image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) floating on green rippled water. The duck in the foreground is larger and sharper, displaying characteristic breeding plumage: iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey body. The second duck is in the background to the right, slightly out of focus but clearly identifiable as a drake with similar coloration. Both exhibit natural floating postures with reflections visible in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both ducks clearly display the characteristic broad, flat, yellow-green bills typical of male mallards. The shape and color are anatomically correct.
Dark eyes are visible on both subjects, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bodies appear streamlined and buoyant, sitting low in the water as expected for aquatic birds. Plumage texture appears dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit the specific Mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey flanks. This matches the ground truth perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ducks are floating on water. Their legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded by the water surface and body angle. It is impossible to verify webbing or leg placement visually.
The wings are folded against the body. The visible portion shows the correct curvature and feather layering consistent with broad, pointed wings at rest.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear duck clearly displays the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers). The foreground duck's tail is partially obscured by angle but appears consistent.
